metadata.title: The Names Nothing Checks
metadata.persona: Synthetic Kokoro af_bella voice reading Weiting Wang's own words (disclosed in the opening beat, on the end card, and in SOURCES.md)
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: show-tell style: opens on the hesitant writer plus the terms card, no verdict card; Your Turn is the Claude.ai composer. The spoken outro stays, but names the author instead of the instructor: the INFO 7375 assignment requires narrating as oneself and forbids the instructor's name, persona or credit line, so the outro handle and narration are the author's. OUTRO-LOCK is expected to flag this; see FRICTIONAL.md.
metadata.audience: Unity gameplay programmers who write code with an AI assistant, and reviewers looking at tools and AI-engineering work
metadata.honesty_note: Nothing in this film exists yet except the Unity game referenced in B09 and B16. Every drawing of the proposed tool is labelled 'proposed' on screen. Past tense appears only in B09 and B16, both of which describe work actually done in spring 2026. Act 2 describes other people's tools; every claim there is quoted from that tool's own documentation and listed in FACTCHECK.md with the page it came from. CORRECTED 2026-10-13: an earlier cut claimed the console says nothing about a wrong animator parameter. Unity does warn about that one. The claim now names the shader property, which Unity's own documentation says has no effect and no message, and B03 states the difference out loud. See FACTCHECK.md rows 3 and 4.
metadata.source_doc: PROJECT-BRIEF.md (this repository, the film's appendix); brutalist.art skills/make/show-tell/SKILL.md

beats.narration_text: Hi. These are Weiting Wang's words, read by a synthetic voice. I build games in Unity. The checks I found ask whether a line of code is fast. The one I am building asks whether the name in it exists.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A shader property: a name stored in a Unity asset, not in the code. A string reference: code reaching that name as quoted text. And a silent failure: wrong code that compiles, runs, and does nothing.

beats.narration_text: I am building a checker for Unity projects. Start with the project itself. One side holds the C sharp scripts. The other holds the assets, and the assets hold the project's real names.

beats.narration_text: What exists already. Unity has solved this once: its Input System can generate a C sharp class from your input actions, so those names become code instead of strings. One name kind out of four.

beats.narration_text: So, how. Step one: read the assets that define names. Shader graphs, animator controllers, the tag manager, the input actions file. Write down every name that really exists.

beats.narration_text: Step two: find every quoted name in the C sharp and compare it against that list. Step three: print what is missing, with the file and the line. It never writes to your project.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude. Pick a project you know well and ask your AI assistant for code that uses a name stored outside the source files: an animator parameter, a shader property, a config key. Then open the file that actually defines that name and compare. Tell me whether the assistant read it or guessed it. Then check two things yourself. Did it say out loud that it was unsure? And would anything in your build have caught it if it was wrong?
